key_insight: An agentic workflow can convert quantum protocols into neutral-atom QPU experiments overnight, while still requiring expert human validation for correctness.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the practical barrier to running quantum hardware campaigns by automating protocol design, compilation, simulation, cloud execution, and feasibility triage.
method: Automated the full pipeline from paper/patent to QPU experiment on Pasqal cloud devices
Kept a human in the loop to validate critical scientific and hardware choices
Used a second agent to screen 633 Rydberg-array arXiv papers for present-day implementability
evidence_signal: In three case studies, the agent produced overnight QPU campaigns, and in a corpus of 633 papers it found that nearly half appear implementable on current hardware.
watch_item: The workflow can generate plausible but wrong choices, so expert review remains necessary for observables and hardware diagnoses.
paper_title: Lowering the implementation barrier of neutral-atom quantum computing with agentic workflows
